body.statement:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), there is one Turing machine extending \(\mathsf E\) with the following properties.  On input \(n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), it outputs an index \(k_n\), the complete verified spline record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), a rational \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}>0\), rational nonnegative errors
\(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and finite ordered-field certificates.  The outputs satisfy
\[
k_n\uparrow\infty,\qquad \varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\downarrow0,\qquad
\alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1.
\]
For
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty\le n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}:\min_a r_a=0\},
\end{aligned}
\]
the certified all-count conclusions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{loc},n}&& (r\in\mathcal L_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{shell},n}&& (r\in\mathcal X_n),\\
G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_{\mathrm{zero},n}&& (r\in\mathcal Z_n).
\end{aligned} \tag{A}
\]
The same output contains a total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) satisfying
\[
\max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
\mathbb E\left[\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-
\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\right]
\le n^{-1}-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}. \tag{B}
\]
It also outputs a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) such that \(E(N)\to0\) and, for every \(n\ge N\),
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N). \tag{C}
\]
The inequalities (A)--(C), including exterior and zero-count control, are theorem conclusions and are not inputs or assumptions.  They imply the finite certified squeeze
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},
\]
and consequently
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]
body.justification: The root theorem is retained as the exact corrected-prior all-count bridge that would convert the finite experiment into the sharp unrestricted second-order value.
body.gap: The compact rational Airy approximation and exact finite evaluator do not imply uniform local, exterior-shell, or zero-face posterior-risk bounds; these must be derived with an effective common error sequence.
body.consumer: A prospective unequal three-regimen binary-endpoint design may use the proved fixed-design benchmark and same-input intervals now; the unrestricted sharp benchmark awaits this theorem.
body.proof_tex:
Use the diagonal search in \(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\).  On input \(n\), generate the complete records supplied by
\(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}normalized\text{-}airy\text{-}record}\) for \(1\leq j\leq n\), put \(\varepsilon_j=2^{-j}\), and choose the largest \(j\) for which
\[
\alpha_n(3T_j^\dagger+2\varepsilon_j)\leq1. \tag{9}
\]
For any fixed \(j\), the quantity \(3T_j^\dagger+2\varepsilon_j\) is finite, whereas \(\alpha_n=n^{-1/3}\to0\).  Thus (9) holds for every sufficiently large \(n\).  It follows first that the admissible set is nonempty for all sufficiently large \(n\), and then, by applying this observation successively to every fixed \(j\), that its maximum \(k_n\) tends to infinity.  The admissible sets can only expand when \(n\) increases, apart from the harmless expanding cap \(j\leq n\); consequently \(k_n\) is nondecreasing.  Hence
\(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}=2^{-k_n}\) is nonincreasing and tends to zero, and (9) is exactly the asserted positivity certificate.

Call finite-input mode with the selected record, \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), and any rational enclosure width, for example \(2^{-n}\).  The conclusion of
\(\mathrm{lem:corrected\text{-}airy\text{-}fixed\text{-}input\text{-}evaluator}\) gives termination, an exact ordered-field representation and rational enclosure of
\(B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), and exact ordered-field maxima of
\(G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\) on each of the three finite allocation strata.  The permutation-orbit Bayes inequality, already included in that lemma's conclusion, gives
\[
R_n(c^\dagger)\geq
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}. \tag{10}
\]

Finally solve the finite rational action-grid program in
\(\mathrm{def:evaluator\text{-}handle}\).  Its feasible optimizer is a total randomized estimator under the outcome-independent design \(q^\dagger\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem:rational\text{-}grid\text{-}primal\text{-}error}\), its risk is at most
\[
\frac1n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
+B_{c^\dagger}n^{-3/2}+\frac1{4\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil^2}.
\]
Since \(\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil^{-2}\leq n^{-3/2}\), this is
\[
\frac1n-
\left\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}\right\}n^{-4/3}. \tag{11}
\]
The rational-grid primal-error lemma further states that the evaluator's rational outward primal error can be chosen so that
\[
e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\leq
(B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Equations (10)--(11) prove every assertion of the narrowed statement.  No convergence claim for any of the three computed Bayes-deficit maxima is used.
